name: mine wall face with ore veins

surfaces.part: dark void or ceiling strip above the wall
dark green wall face with ore veins
brown dirt floor in front of the wall

answer.evidence: The wall has a light gray ledge in rows 9-16 (lighter speckled stone, about 8 rows). It ends in a darker edge line at row 17 (L=89), followed by darker rows from 18 that read as eave shadow. Below that is a tall dark green wall face, rows 18-63 (about 46 rows), holding gold and silver ore veins. Rows 62-63 form a dark base shadow, and a flat dirt floor fills rows 64-95. The silhouette is a constant 112 px wide, as expected for a terrain tile block. The wall reads as a wall with a top ledge and a front face, not a flat slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has about 10 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving reference, so it is at or above both. Near-flat coverage is 7%, and the exact 5x5 flat fill is 0%. The dark rock face is mottled with stone patches, and the gold and iron ore clusters have highlights. The dirt floor strip has dense speckle grain in several browns, and the stone ledge is shaded. The 84% near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is close to the paving reference's 80%, which is neutral grey stone. In the picture the dark edges on the rock face and ore read as slightly tinted, so I call the outline mixed rather than near_black. The candidate does lean on dark tones around the ore and top band, but the material ramps hold about 5 steps each, comparable to the references. Structure and texture are in line with the Beodeul standard.

Rows 62-63 are a dark base line, and a separate brown dirt floor fills rows 64-95. The wall has a top ledge and a tall vertical front face, so it reads as three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 10 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving reference and 3 for the grass reference, and 7% near-flat coverage against 0% for both references, so it is not shallow on the primary facts. The wall face has a dark base with mottled darker and lighter patches, gold and grey ore clusters with highlights, a light stone cap strip, and a soil strip with speckled grain in several browns. The 84% near-neutral dark edge share is close to the paving reference's 80%, and the paving reference passes with its grey stone. Forms are separated mainly by value, with some dark outlines around the ore. The dark wall face has some larger smooth areas, and the ore veins are small and sparse, so overall texture is some rather than rich. A careful artist would accept it next to the references.

answer.evidence: Rows 0-8 are dark void behind the wall. Rows 9-16 are a lighter speckled stone band, the top surface of the wall. It ends in a darker front-edge line at row 17 (L≈89), followed by darker eave shadow in rows 18-19. Below that, rows 18-63 are the dark green vertical front face (46 rows) carrying gold and silver ore veins, ending in a dark base line at rows 62-63. Rows 64-95 are the flat brown floor tile. The wall therefore has a top band plus a front face of 3+ rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts favour the candidate. It has 10 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving and 3 for the grass. Near-flat coverage is 7% against 0% for both references. The brown soil band is speckled and grained with about 5 lightness steps. The grey top band and the wall face have subtle block variation, and the gold and grey ore nuggets carry several tones each. Dark edge pixels are 84% near-neutral, but the paving reference is 80% neutral on its grey stone, so this does not clearly mark a sticker look. The near-black strip at the top and the dark neutral edges on the ore nuggets pull the outline toward near_black, so I rate it mixed. The wall face is the weakest area. It is a dark, fairly even field with sparse texture and only about 3-4 steps, and the ore clusters sit on it somewhat like stickers. Overall it is about at the reference level for density and texture, so it passes narrowly.
